source_anchor_evidence.quoted_text:
We assume that within each Borough, the server is managed with the Generalized Processor Sharing (GPS) scheme \citep{parekh1993generalized}. {We use the ideal-fluid, preemptive-resume version of GPS and evaluate long-run response times after the system has reached steady operation.} Under the GPS scheme, each SLA category is assigned a weight $\phi_{k,b}$ in each Borough $b$, such that $\sum_{k\in \mathcal{S}}\phi_{k,b} \leq 1$. At any given time $t$, on a server with capacity $C_b$, the (potentially fractional)

capacity devoted to category $k \in \mathcal{S}$ is $C_b\phi_{k,b}/\sum_{k'\in \mathcal{K}_b(t)}\phi_{k',b}$, where $\mathcal{K}_b(t)$ denotes the set of categories for which there is at least one pending incident (there is a ``backlog'' of incidents) in Borough $b$. {Thus, every backlogged category $k$ receives service at rate at least $C_b\phi_{k,b}$. }To finish formally describing the system, as standard in such queuing systems \citep{liu2001maximizing}, we assume that there is an additional category of work that is always backlogged for which the city provides no guarantees---the worker services this category when there is no backlog in categories $k \in \mathcal{S}$. Within each queue, we assume a first-come-first-served (FCFS) discipline of service. At a high level, $\phi_{k,b}$ determines the relative priority of different incident categories within a Borough---for example, a \textit{Hazard} category may be higher risk on average, and so prioritized on average.

which we will henceforth refer to as the ``SLA constraint.'' Intuitively, this constraint states that: when $C_b$ budget is allocated to Borough $b$, and category $k$ is assigned a GPS parameter $\phi_{k,b}$, then at least $\frac{s_{k,b}}{\lambda_{k,b}}(1-\alpha_{k,b})$ fraction of all category $k$ requests in Borough $b$ should be {responded to} within $z_{k,b}$ days, i.e., the SLA would be $z_{k,b}$ days. Practically, enforcing the same tail constraint for all categories enhances the interpretability of the policy,

thus we will consider {$\alpha_{k,b}=\bar\alpha$ and write $a=-\log(\bar\alpha)$} for all category--Borough cells $(k,b)$, which also simplifies notations. Note that {$\bar\alpha\in(0,1)$}, and so {$a>0$}. In the appendix, we prove some of the statements using general $a_{k,b}$.

source_anchor_evidence.quoted_text:
The queuing network within each Borough operates as follows. We have a set of incident categories $k \in \mathcal{S}$ (e.g., Hazards versus less urgent incidents) for which we wish to define SLAs. Each category arrives according to a {Poisson process} with rate $\lambda_{k,b} > 0 $ into their own queues, where each of these Poisson processes are mutually independent. In practice, not every incident is responded to; we model this as incidents being  dropped (independently) with probability $1 - \pi_{k,b} \in [0, 1)$, and define non-dropped incident rate as $s_{k,b}=\lambda_{k,b}\pi_{k,b}$.

By independent thinning, admitted requests form independent Poisson processes of rates $s_{k,b}>0$.

Inspecting each incident takes up a random amount of time, {with iid unit-mean exponential service time, independent of other events.} {(And can be extended to different processing times by category).}

source_anchor_evidence.quoted_text:
For our theoretical results, it will be convenient to define a benchmark-specific effective-load index for the
efficiency-maximizing solution,
$A_{\mathrm{eff}}(s) =\sum_{k,b}\sqrt{a s_{k,b}r_{k,b}}$.\footnote{Any reduced problem of the form
$\min_x\sum_i c_i x_i$ subject to $\sum_i d_i/x_i\leq E$ has optimal variable
cost $(\sum_i\sqrt{c_i d_i})^2/E$, and so $A_{\mathrm{eff}}$ captures the
cost component corresponding to inspected incidents.}

source_anchor_evidence.quoted_text:
The most equitable solution minimizes
\begin{equation*}
 F(s,z)=\sum_k\left[\max_b\operatorname{Cost}_{k,b}(s,z)
 -\min_b\operatorname{Cost}_{k,b}(s,z)\right] \geq0
\end{equation*}
given the constraint in Eq.~\eqref{opt-reformulated}.  Write $\operatorname{Cost}_{k,b}(s,z)=c_{k,b}z_{k,b}+d_{k,b}$, where
\begin{equation*}
 c_{k,b}=\frac{s_{k,b}r_{k,b}}{\lambda_{k,b}}>0,
 \qquad
 d_{k,b}=\left(1-\frac{s_{k,b}}{\lambda_{k,b}}\right)r_{k,b}D_{k,b},
\end{equation*}  For any
$M_k>\max_b d_{k,b}$, setting $z_{k,b}=\frac{M_k-d_{k,b}}{c_{k,b}}$
gives $\operatorname{Cost}_{k,b}(s,z)=M_k$.  As every $M_k$ increases, so does $z_{k,b}$. Thus,
$\sum_{k,b}a/z_{k,b}$ converges to zero, so these thresholds can be chosen to
satisfy Eq.~\eqref{opt-reformulated}.  Thus the minimum equity loss is zero,
which proves the stated categorywise equality. Note that we can then show that the efficiency-best solution among solutions equalizing costs exists, due to continuity of $G$ and compactness in $z$ (which is lower bounded due to the feasibility constraint; then, a single solution to the equity minimizing optimization produces a sublevel set for $G$, bounding $z$ from above.) Finally, note that the constraint binds at the efficiency-best equitable solution (otherwise, we can perturb $z$ to improve the efficiency loss while keeping the equity loss at $0$.)

source_anchor_evidence.quoted_text:
For either endpoint policy $z^j$ for $j\in\{\mathrm{eff},\mathrm{eq}\}$, let $q^j=q(z^j)$ denote the fraction of total capacity slack $E(s)$ assigned to category--Borough cell $(k,b)$, where
$q_{k,b}(z^j)=\frac{a}{E(s)z^j_{k,b}}$\footnote{The supporting policy satisfies $\phi_{k,b}C_b=s_{k,b}+a/z_{k,b}$, so $a/z_{k,b}$ is the cell's guaranteed service-rate margin above its admitted load.  Because the reciprocal-capacity constraint binds, these margins sum to $E(s)$; hence
$q_{k,b}(z)=(a/z_{k,b})/E(s)$.} For probability vectors $P$ and $Q$, let the Pearson chi-square divergence be $\chi^2(P\|Q)=\sum_{k,b}(P_{k,b}-Q_{k,b})^2/Q_{k,b}$.

approved_review_contexts.checked_scope: The direct admitted arrival/work and stationary Palm constructions are checked through the active queueing route. The convention covers only the source-stated admitted-stream normal form. It does not assert a raw-path or empirical-frequency theorem, and it does not credit an unproved raw-to-admitted transport.
approved_review_contexts.formal_meaning: The source itself states the independent admitted Poisson streams at rates s after thinning, together with iid unit-mean exponential work. The active Lean route constructs that admitted-stream/Palm model directly at the stated rates and uses it for GPS/FCFS replay.
approved_review_contexts.why_needed: The source writes the admitted-stream law explicitly, but the current library does not yet prove a pathwise raw-marked survivor re-enumeration, multiclass pushforward equality, selected-Palm transport, and response-functional correspondence. Calling the direct carrier a derivation from the raw carrier would therefore be false; taking the explicitly stated post-thinning law as the model normal form is precise and does not weaken a named paper conclusion.

approved_review_contexts.checked_scope: PaperInterface.lean makes both the global steady-operation condition and the target-local margin visible. SLA2026GPSParameters.lean derives the stronger all-cell/aggregate facts only inside the fixed-load-feasible policy bridge. The stationary selected-Palm GPS/FCFS proof uses the visible global condition plus the target margin and does not treat the fixed-load bridge as an unconditional source derivation.
approved_review_contexts.formal_meaning: For the selected Borough's SLA subsystem, Lean makes explicit the full-system well-definedness regularity implicit in the source's GPS/steady-operation language: nonnegative capacity, positive SLA weights, total weight at most one, and total SLA admitted load below capacity. The displayed target tail margin remains the separate condition s_target < C phi_target. Always-backlogged no-guarantee background work is excluded from the SLA load sum because it receives only residual capacity.

approved_review_contexts.why_needed: The standalone display explicitly states only the target-local margin, while the active remote-past construction needs a stable full SLA subsystem. The source's positive admitted streams and GPS active-set allocation make zero weight for any SLA class incompatible with a well-defined stationary full queue, and aggregate slack is needed for stationarity. The later fixed-load program proves stronger all-cell margins only for policies satisfying its own quantified SLA constraints, together with the positive SLA parameter recorded at :600-602; it cannot silently strengthen the standalone display. This convention exposes the implicit global regularity and keeps its dependency direction honest.

The displayed target-local margin is s_{k,b} < C_b phi_{k,b}.
